LESSON: ELECTRICAL ENERGY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: INTEGRAT ED SCIENCE
Strand: Force and Energy
Topic 4.1: Electrical Energy
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Electrical Energy, part of Force and Energy in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven INTEGRAT ED SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: how to interpret tactile 1. Why do we observe safety measures when handling electrical appliances?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Electrical Energy together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: The learner leans how to set up a simple electric circuit as they carry out activities of series and in

parallel circuits.

● Communication and collaboration: The learner collaboratively works with peers to set up simple electrical circuits

in series and in parallel.

Values:
● Unity: The learner works harmoniously as they set up simple electrical circuits in series and parallel in groups.

● Patriotism: The learner exercises dedication in setting up simple electrical circuits in series and parallel in groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social economic and environmental issues: The learner exercises safety and security in the class and school environment as they

identify and discuss safety measures to follow when using electrical appliances.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: how to interpret tactile 1. Why do we observe safety measures when handling electrical appliances?
